pages.text: "Silly Momo! Go away!" Yuki shouted. Momo had stepped on the sun Yuki was drawing in the yard's soil. The brown dog laid their ears down and backed away.
"We'll play tag when I finish!" Yuki drew the sun again with a stick. Momo stood far away, tail lowered.
When Momo approached, Yuki shouted again. "Don't step on it! Slowpoke, move!" Momo folded their ears and slipped beneath the porch.
Finishing the picture, Yuki called, "Let's play tag!" But Momo would not come out.
"Why won't Momo come?" Yuki looked sad. Sorting beans, Grandma said, "Momo can't speak, but hears everything. The tail answers."
Yuki crouched beneath the porch and spoke softly. "I'm sorry about earlier." A nose poked from the dim space.
"Let's play. You're the fastest in our house!" Momo's tail waved gently. "Kind Words, a Wagging Tail!"
Momo darted out and circled the yard. Laughing, Yuki chased. When called, Momo came, again and again.
The next day, Momo stepped on the drawing again. Yuki swallowed the sharp words, fixed the scarf knot, and called kindly. "One, swallow hurtful words! Two, say the name kindly! Three, sorry first!"
Yuki buried their face in Momo's back. Kind words made the tail answer first. "Kind Words, a Wagging Tail! Right, Momo?"
